open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict” conflicts with “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time, and the verdict covers exactly those executions”; those TrialExecutions have independently minted identities, and `decided_at` also differs.
open_points.question: Is an admission verdict one reusable value per implementation and corpus, or is each admission evaluation a distinct record with its own executions and decision time?
options: One value per implementation and corpus; later submissions reuse the original verdict and evidence
A distinct entity for every admission evaluation
A stable logical verdict plus separate admission-evaluation records containing executions and time
open_points.default_guess: Treat each admission evaluation as a distinct entity so its exact TrialExecutions and decision time remain immutable.

open_points.subject: M17 ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with the carried statement that “a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can produce different results as referenced bindings change status?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant dependency state or snapshot
Each proof invocation is a distinct entity
Proof is fixed on first computation, requiring a new flow version after dependencies change
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computation as an on-demand value identified by its complete result and the dependency state under which it was computed, not by `flow_version_id` alone.
